title: Provenance Event
description: One asset's state within one run. Records the producer (producer_*) and the consumer (actor_*) on the same row; this cannot be backfilled, because asset ownership changes and versions roll forward.

event_id.description: Stable id, referenced by gate-decision.evidence_refs and by receipts. Derived from session_key + asset_id + state + occurred_at.

state.description: recalled: the asset entered the candidate set for this turn. selected: it survived selection and was chosen for the context. injected: its content or a callable reference to it appears in the request the model received. fetched: the model actively retrieved this specific asset's content, evidenced by a call that names it and returns it. used: hard evidence matched and a fetch of that same asset preceded it. used_soft: only soft evidence (a model judgement) matched, which is not enough to promote to used. needs_review: a token matched but no fetch of that asset preceded it, so the model may have known it from elsewhere. validated: used, and the acceptance check tied to that asset's own call passed. corrected: counter-evidence tied to that asset's own call.

session_key.description: Normalised session id (client prefix such as 'codebuddy:' removed).

run_id.description: Run id assigned by the E2E runner; may be null for historical fetch-level events.

task_id.description: Evaluation task id; generalisation is counted as distinct values of this field.

occurred_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC, taken from the service-side record's timestamp.

asset_version.description: Asset version at the moment of the event. Together with run_id and asset_id this is the lookup key for tracing any conclusion back to its evidence.

pool_snapshot_at.description: The instant the asset pool was frozen. Assets created after it must be flagged with excluded_by_snapshot.

excluded_by_snapshot.description: true = the asset was created after the pool was frozen and is excluded from all statistics (answer-leak guard).

actor_user_id.description: The user_id of the session that performed this run.

actor_agent_id.description: The agent_id of the session that performed this run.

relation.description: Derived from producer/actor. Reports unknown when either identity is missing; never defaults to self.

observation.description: How the event was witnessed, not how strong the claim is. bridge+wire: a service-side record and the capture both show it. bridge_only: service-side record only. wire_only: capture only. Doubtful for fetched and beyond, because the capture is reconstructed from model-produced text; not doubtful for injected, because the capture is taken upstream of the proxy, so an injected block there was written by the proxy and the model could not have produced it. none: nothing was observed (occurs only with needs_review, where a token matched but nothing was ever fetched).

content_delivered.description: Whether the response actually carried the asset's body. A non-enumeration endpoint is not enough: `get` with include_content:false returns id, name and version only, and `update` returns a metadata summary — both would otherwise look like retrieval. True only when the captured response was inspected and found to carry content. False when it was inspected and did not. Null when the response was never captured, which is not the same as false and must not be read as either delivery or its absence.

context_entry_index.description: Position in the session's message sequence at which this asset's content entered the model's context — the index of the message carrying the response, not of the call that asked for it. Ordering must be judged on this rather than on wall-clock time: a model can emit several tool calls in one message, so two calls share a timestamp while the second was written before the first one's result existed. Null when the delivering message was not observed.

evidence_tier.description: How strong the 'it was used' judgement is. hard: a discriminative token from the asset appears in the run's artifacts. soft: a model judged an asset claim related to the change. Null while state is fetched.

target_type.description: Present from state=used onward: what the asset affected.

proof_refs.description: Resolvable evidence references; sensitive content is not copied. Must be non-empty from state=fetched onward. For fetched and beyond, at least one ref must identify the specific asset — a bridge_response naming this asset_id, or a bridge_row whose request targets it by name or id. A successful call elsewhere in the same session is not evidence that this asset was retrieved.

corrected_reason.description: Set only when state=corrected. Only wrong / stale feed the down-weighting path.

ref.description: An id, path or hash that resolves back to the original record.

detail.description: Optional human-readable note, such as the token that matched.
